title: Kerch Bridge strike, Voyager's light-day milestone and GTA VI leave

stories.headline: Ukraine badly damages Russia's Kerch Bridge to Crimea
stories.headlineZh: 乌克兰重创连接克里米亚与俄罗斯的刻赤大桥
stories.summaryZh: 乌克兰连续两天袭击刻赤大桥，公路段疑似坍塌，距和谈仅一周。
stories.c1:
Ukraine has inflicted what appears to be serious damage on the Crimean Bridge, the 19-kilometre road and rail link that connects southern Russia with the occupied peninsula. Images circulated by Ukrainian officials seemed to show a section of the road span lying in the water after a second consecutive day of attacks, while Ukraine's General Staff said the rail section was still standing, albeit with a damaged arch.

The bridge carries enormous symbolic weight. It is closely associated with Vladimir Putin, who oversaw Russia's annexation of Crimea in 2014, so any successful strike on it is likely to be read as a political blow as much as a military one. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy presented the attack as retaliation for Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure. Moscow's installed governor in Crimea said two people had been killed, and traffic across the crossing was suspended. The Kremlin, for its part, insisted that a repair plan would be drawn up and that the bridge would emerge stronger than before.

The strike coincided with what Russian state media described as the largest Ukrainian drone attack since the full-scale invasion in 2022, with Russia's Defence Ministry claiming to have shot down 1,441 drones over 22 regions. Russia, meanwhile, hit bridges, energy facilities and part of the metro in Kyiv, and overnight strikes left consumers in eight Ukrainian regions without power.

Perhaps the most sobering aspect is the timing. The escalation came only a week after US-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi, the first in nine months. Both sides now appear to be targeting each other's energy and transport networks in a grinding war of attrition, which suggests that, for the time being, neither is prepared to make the concessions a lasting deal would require.
stories.b2:
Ukraine has seriously damaged the Crimean Bridge, a 19-kilometre road and rail link between southern Russia and occupied Crimea. Pictures shared by Ukrainian officials seemed to show part of the road section in the water after two days of attacks. Ukraine's military said the rail section was still standing, but its arch was damaged.

The bridge is an important symbol. It is closely linked to Vladimir Putin, who led Russia's annexation of Crimea in 2014. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the attack was a response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure. Russia's governor in Crimea said two people were killed, and traffic on the bridge was stopped. The Kremlin said it would prepare a plan to repair the bridge.

At the same time, Russian state media reported the biggest Ukrainian drone attack since 2022. Russia's Defence Ministry said it shot down 1,441 drones over 22 regions. Russia also hit bridges, energy sites and part of the metro in Kyiv, and people in eight Ukrainian regions lost power.

The timing is worrying. The attacks came just one week after US-led peace talks in Abu Dhabi, the first in nine months. Both countries are now attacking each other's energy and transport systems, and neither seems ready to compromise.

vocab.en: to cause something harmful to happen to someone or something
vocab.example: The storm inflicted heavy losses on local farmers.

vocab.en: although; even if (used to add a limiting detail)
vocab.example: The plan worked, albeit more slowly than we had hoped.

vocab.en: importance that comes from what something represents
vocab.example: The old town hall carries real symbolic weight for residents.

vocab.en: to be interpreted in a particular way
vocab.example: His silence could easily be read as agreement.

vocab.en: action taken to harm someone who has harmed you
vocab.example: The new tariffs were imposed in retaliation for earlier trade restrictions.

vocab.en: to come out of a difficult situation in a better state
vocab.example: Many small businesses emerged stronger from the downturn.

vocab.en: to happen at the same time as something else
vocab.example: The festival coincides with the school holidays this year.

vocab.en: making you feel serious and think carefully
vocab.example: The report offers a sobering picture of youth unemployment.

vocab.en: a long conflict in which each side tries to wear the other down
vocab.example: The pay dispute has turned into a war of attrition between management and staff.

questions.q: The rail section of the bridge collapsed into the water.
questions.explain: 文中说 "the rail section was still standing, albeit with a damaged arch"，铁路段仍然矗立，所以错误。

questions.q: Zelenskyy said the attack was a response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure.
questions.explain: 文中说 Zelenskyy "presented the attack as retaliation for Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure"，与题干一致。

questions.q: Russian engineers expect repairs to take at least a year.
questions.explain: 文中只提到 "a repair plan would be drawn up"，没有提及修复所需时间。

questions.q: What does the writer find most sobering about the attacks?
options: The record number of drones involved
That they came soon after peace talks
The number of people killed on the bridge
The cost of repairing the bridge
questions.explain: 文中说 "the most sobering aspect is the timing"，即袭击发生在 Abu Dhabi 和谈后仅一周。

stories.discuss: Why do you think leaders often target symbolic structures during conflicts? Can such attacks make peace harder or easier to achieve?

stories.headline: Voyager 1 set to reach one light-day from Earth
stories.headlineZh: 旅行者1号即将抵达距地球一光日之处
stories.summaryZh: 发射近50年后，旅行者1号将距地球约259亿公里，信号单程需24小时。
stories.c1:
Nearly half a century after leaving Earth, NASA's Voyager 1 is poised to pass a remarkable milestone: on 18 November it is expected to become the first human-made object to sit one light-day from home. At roughly 25.9 billion kilometres away, a radio signal sent from Earth would take a full 24 hours to reach the probe, and any reply would need just as long to make the return journey.

Launched in 1977 alongside its twin, Voyager 2, the spacecraft was originally intended to last about a decade. Instead, it toured Jupiter and Saturn, crossed into interstellar space in 2012 and is still hurtling outward at about 61,000 kilometres per hour. Voyager 2, which also flew past Uranus and Neptune, followed it into interstellar space in 2018, but is not expected to reach the same distance until 2035.

That said, the ageing explorer is living on borrowed time. Most of its instruments have been switched off, only two remain operational, and its thrusters are gradually clogging. Last month NASA lost contact with it for roughly 48 hours before it eventually came back online, a reminder of just how fragile the connection has become. Power and heating could last until the early 2030s, although that is far from guaranteed.

Arguably, Voyager's legacy extends well beyond the data it has gathered. Its images of Jupiter made distant worlds feel tangible to many people, and each probe carries a golden record of greetings, music and sounds from Earth, which scientists believe may outlast human civilisation itself. Project scientist Linda Spilker described the moment as an "incredible milestone to celebrate".
stories.b2:
Almost 50 years after leaving Earth, NASA's Voyager 1 is about to reach an amazing milestone. On 18 November, it is expected to be one light-day from Earth. That is about 25.9 billion kilometres, so a radio signal from Earth would need 24 hours to reach the probe.

Voyager 1 was launched in 1977 with its twin, Voyager 2. It was planned to work for about ten years. Instead, it visited Jupiter and Saturn, entered interstellar space in 2012 and is still travelling at about 61,000 kilometres per hour. Voyager 2 also visited Uranus and Neptune and entered interstellar space in 2018. It is expected to reach one light-day in 2035.

However, Voyager 1 is getting old. Most of its instruments are switched off, only two still work, and its thrusters are slowly becoming blocked. Last month, NASA lost contact with it for about 48 hours before it came back online. Its power and heating may last until the early 2030s.

Voyager is important for more than science. Its pictures of Jupiter made faraway planets feel real to many people. Each probe also carries a golden record with greetings, music and sounds from Earth. Scientists think this record may last longer than human civilisation.

vocab.example: The company is poised to announce record profits.

vocab.en: an important stage or event in a process
vocab.example: Finishing her first marathon was a real milestone for her.

vocab.en: to move very fast, often in a way that seems dangerous
vocab.example: The train hurtled past the platform without stopping.

vocab.en: to continue to exist longer than expected, but likely to end soon
vocab.example: Our old laptop is living on borrowed time, so we'd better back everything up.

vocab.en: working and ready to be used
vocab.example: The new hospital wing will be fully operational by March.

vocab.en: to start working or be connected again after a failure
vocab.example: The website came back online after a two-hour outage.

vocab.en: not at all certain
vocab.example: Funding for the project is far from guaranteed.

vocab.en: real and able to be understood or felt
vocab.example: The programme has delivered tangible benefits for local families.

vocab.en: to continue to exist for longer than something else
vocab.example: Good friendships often outlast the jobs that bring people together.

questions.q: Voyager 2 will reach one light-day from Earth before 2030.
questions.explain: 文中说 Voyager 2 "is not expected to reach the same distance until 2035"，所以错误。

questions.q: NASA is planning a new mission to follow Voyager 1 into interstellar space.
questions.explain: 文中没有提到任何新的探测任务。

questions.q: Voyager 1 was originally expected to operate for around ten years.
questions.explain: 文中说它 "was originally intended to last about a decade"，一个十年即约十年。

questions.q: Why does the writer mention that NASA lost contact with Voyager 1 last month?
options: To show that the probe is travelling faster than expected
To explain why the instruments were switched off
To show how fragile the connection has become
To suggest that the mission will end this year
questions.explain: 文中说失联约48小时是 "a reminder of just how fragile the connection has become"。

stories.discuss: Why do you think people feel so attached to old space missions like Voyager? Should governments keep funding missions that have already achieved their main goals?

stories.headline: Bunnings to cut 230 tech jobs in offshoring deal
stories.headlineZh: Bunnings将裁减230个技术岗位并外包海外
stories.summaryZh: Bunnings把大部分技术服务交给印度塔塔咨询，约230个长期岗位将被裁撤。
stories.c1:
Bunnings, the hardware chain that has become something of an Australian institution, will axe about 230 permanent technology roles and end a further 120 contractor positions as it hands much of its tech work to India-based Tata Consultancy Services (TCS). Under the restructure, the retailer will retain a core in-house team of about 500 people in Australia, while the remaining services will be delivered by TCS staff in Australia, India and the Philippines.

The transition is set to begin in December and run until June 2027, with job losses starting in the new year. Bunnings says affected employees will be offered redundancy packages, career transition help, wellbeing support and, where possible, redeployment. Managing director Mike Schneider described the move as a necessary change aimed at responding to evolving consumer needs.

Breaking the news to staff in a virtual meeting, chief information officer Genevie Elliott stressed that the cuts were no reflection on individual performance. She argued that the partnership would help rein in costs and give the business access to specialist expertise and global retail experience at a time when online shopping and technology are changing rapidly.

Bunnings is hardly alone. Qantas, NAB, Officeworks, Woolworths and Coles have all announced overseas outsourcing in some form. While companies tend to justify such decisions on the grounds of efficiency, the trend inevitably raises awkward questions about the future of skilled white-collar work in Australia, and about whether the savings will ultimately benefit customers or simply flow through to profits.
stories.b2:
Bunnings, the popular Australian hardware chain, will cut about 230 permanent technology jobs and end 120 contractor roles. It is moving much of its tech work to Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), a company based in India. Bunnings will keep a team of about 500 tech workers in Australia, and TCS staff in Australia, India and the Philippines will do the rest.

The change will start in December and continue until June 2027. Job losses will begin in the new year. Bunnings says workers will get redundancy packages, help with finding new careers, wellbeing support and, where possible, other jobs in the company. Managing director Mike Schneider said the change was necessary to respond to changing customer needs.

Chief information officer Genevie Elliott told staff about the cuts in an online meeting. She said the decision had nothing to do with how well individual people had worked. She said working with TCS would reduce costs and give Bunnings access to expert knowledge and global retail experience.

Bunnings is not the only company doing this. Qantas, NAB, Officeworks, Woolworths and Coles have also moved some work overseas. Companies say it makes them more efficient, but the trend raises questions about the future of skilled office jobs in Australia.

vocab.en: to suddenly remove jobs, services or plans
vocab.example: The council plans to axe two bus routes next year.

vocab.en: done by a company's own staff rather than outside workers
vocab.example: We have an in-house design team, so we rarely use agencies.

vocab.en: money and benefits given to workers whose jobs are cut
vocab.example: She used her redundancy package to retrain as a nurse.

vocab.en: moving staff to a different job within the same organisation
vocab.example: The union is pushing for redeployment rather than job losses.

vocab.en: to tell someone important, often bad, news
vocab.example: He broke the news to his parents that he was leaving uni.

vocab.en: not a sign that someone has done badly
vocab.example: Not getting the grant is no reflection on the quality of your work.

vocab.en: to control or limit something, especially spending
vocab.example: The government has promised to rein in public spending.

vocab.en: because of; for the reason of
vocab.example: The application was rejected on the grounds of cost.

vocab.en: to make people ask difficult or uncomfortable things

questions.q: The union representing Bunnings staff has strongly criticised the decision.
questions.explain: 文中没有提到工会的反应。

questions.q: Bunnings will keep a team of about 500 technology workers in Australia.
questions.explain: 文中说 Bunnings "will retain a core in-house team of about 500 people in Australia"。

questions.q: All of the outsourced work will be carried out in India.
questions.explain: 文中说服务将由 "TCS staff in Australia, India and the Philippines" 提供，并非全部在印度。

questions.q: According to Genevie Elliott, what is one benefit of the partnership with TCS?
options: Higher wages for the remaining staff
Access to specialist expertise and global retail experience
questions.explain: 文中说合作会带来 "access to specialist expertise and global retail experience"。

stories.discuss: Why do you think so many large companies are moving work overseas? What could governments or workers do in response?

stories.headline: Australians take time off work for Grand Theft Auto VI
stories.headlineZh: 澳洲玩家纷纷请假迎接《侠盗猎车手6》
stories.summaryZh: 《侠盗猎车手6》即将发售，许多澳洲玩家请年假抢先体验，网络流量大增。
stories.c1:
Australians are not usually known for taking annual leave to stay indoors, yet that is precisely what many fans are doing for Grand Theft Auto VI, which launches on Thursday morning after years of delays and leaks. Rather than wait for the weekend, devoted players are booking days off so they can lose themselves in the game's fictional, Florida-inspired setting, which includes Vice City, a stand-in for Miami.

The sheer scale of the project is hard to overstate. Reviewer Ben Schuster estimates its budget at between US$1.5 billion and US$2 billion, which would make it the most expensive video game ever made. Analytics firm Sensor Tower reports almost 15 million pre-orders, and Forbes expects the game to earn nearly $4.5 billion in its opening week. Its predecessor, GTA V, has sold more than 255 million copies since its release in 2013.

Even the internet has felt the strain. Since downloads opened on 10 November, the NBN has recorded a noticeable jump in network use, with a spokesperson noting that the download alone is roughly 40 per cent of what an average home uses in a month. One fan, who has spent more than 3,000 hours on the previous instalment, has taken four days off and intends to finish the story before returning to work, largely to avoid spoilers.

Not everyone is entirely comfortable with this enthusiasm. Responding to concerns that some workers might call in sick to play, the Fair Work Ombudsman reminded employees that employers are entitled to ask for evidence when sick leave is claimed. Still, with Schuster pointing out that 82 per cent of Australians play video games, the release is arguably less a niche event than a genuine cultural moment.
stories.b2:
Many Australian fans are taking annual leave to play Grand Theft Auto VI, which comes out on Thursday morning after years of delays and leaks. They are booking days off to explore the game's fictional world, which is based on Florida.

The game is a huge project. Reviewer Ben Schuster thinks it cost between US$1.5 billion and US$2 billion to make, which would make it the most expensive video game ever. Sensor Tower says there have been almost 15 million pre-orders, and Forbes expects the game to earn nearly $4.5 billion in its first week. The last game, GTA V, has sold more than 255 million copies since 2013.

Downloads started on 10 November, and the NBN saw a clear rise in internet use. A spokesperson said the download is about 40 per cent of what an average home uses in a month. One fan, who has played more than 3,000 hours of the last game, has taken four days off to finish the story and avoid spoilers.

Some people worry that workers might call in sick to play. The Fair Work Ombudsman reminded workers that employers can ask for evidence when someone takes sick leave. Still, with 82 per cent of Australians playing video games, the release is a real cultural event.

vocab.en: to become so involved in something that you forget everything else
vocab.example: On long flights I like to lose myself in a good novel.

vocab.en: a person or thing that takes the place of another
vocab.example: The fictional town in the series is a stand-in for Hobart.

vocab.en: so important or large that it is difficult to exaggerate
vocab.example: The importance of clean water is hard to overstate.

vocab.en: something or someone that came before another
vocab.example: The new phone is lighter than its predecessor.

vocab.en: to be affected by pressure or heavy demand
vocab.example: Hospitals are feeling the strain during flu season.

vocab.en: one part of a series of films, books or games
vocab.example: The final instalment of the trilogy comes out next year.

vocab.en: to phone work to say you are ill and cannot come in
vocab.example: Half the team called in sick after the end-of-year party.

vocab.en: to have the right to do or have something
vocab.example: Casual workers are entitled to a higher hourly rate.

vocab.en: interesting to or aimed at only a small group of people
vocab.example: The shop sells niche products for keen home brewers.

questions.q: Downloads of the game became available on 10 November.
questions.explain: 文中说 "downloads opened on 10 November"，与题干一致。

questions.q: Most fans intend to play the game online with friends.
questions.explain: 文中没有提到大多数玩家是否与朋友联机游戏。

questions.q: The Fair Work Ombudsman has banned workers from taking sick leave to play the game.
questions.explain: 监察署只是提醒 "employers are entitled to ask for evidence when sick leave is claimed"，并没有禁止。

questions.q: Why does one fan plan to finish the game before going back to work?
options: Because the download takes four days
Because the game will be more expensive later
To review it for a magazine
questions.explain: 文中说这位玩家想在返工前打通剧情 "largely to avoid spoilers"。

stories.discuss: Why do you think some entertainment releases become shared cultural events? Is it reasonable to take annual leave for something like a game or a concert?

dialogue.title: Interview Nerves over Coffee
dialogue.setting: Callum, who has a job interview the next morning, gets some last-minute advice from a friend at a café in Brunswick.
dialogue.settingZh: Callum第二天早上有个求职面试，在布伦瑞克的一家咖啡馆向朋友讨教临场建议。

lines.name: Callum
lines.en: Thanks for coming, Ines. My interview's at nine tomorrow and I'm a bit of a wreck.
lines.zh: 谢谢你过来，Ines。我明天九点有那个面试，我现在紧张得要命。

lines.name: Ines
lines.en: No worries. Grab a flat white and let's run through the questions you're dreading.
lines.zh: 没事。点杯馥芮白，我们把你最怕的问题过一遍。

lines.name: Callum
lines.en: Mainly the 'tell me about yourself' one. I always end up rambling about my whole life.
lines.zh: 主要是“介绍一下你自己”那题。我每次都会把整个人生絮絮叨叨讲一遍。

lines.name: Ines
lines.en: Keep it to two minutes, tops. Where you are now, what you've done, and why this role.
lines.zh: 最多两分钟。讲讲你现在的情况、做过什么，以及为什么想要这个职位。

lines.name: Callum
lines.en: Right. What if they ask about the gap in my CV? I took six months off.
lines.zh: 好。那如果他们问我简历上的空档怎么办？我休了六个月。

lines.name: Ines
lines.en: Just own it. Say you went travelling and came back with a clearer sense of direction.
lines.zh: 大方承认就好。说你去旅行了，回来后方向更清晰了。

lines.name: Callum
lines.en: I'm also worried they'll throw a curly technical question at me.
lines.zh: 我还担心他们会抛给我一个刁钻的技术问题。

lines.name: Ines
lines.en: If you're stumped, talk them through how you'd tackle it. They want to see how you think.
lines.zh: 要是被难住了，就跟他们讲讲你会怎么解决。他们想看你的思路。

lines.name: Callum
lines.en: That's a good shout. Should I ask them anything at the end, or is that pushy?
lines.zh: 好主意。最后我该向他们提问吗？还是会显得有点咄咄逼人？

lines.name: Ines
lines.en: Definitely ask something. Maybe what success would look like in the first six months.
lines.zh: 一定要问点什么。比如头六个月里怎样才算做得好。

lines.name: Callum
lines.en: Ooh, I like that. It shows I'm already picturing myself in the job.
lines.zh: 哦，这个好。说明我已经在想象自己做这份工作了。

lines.name: Ines
lines.en: Exactly. And for heaven's sake, get a decent night's sleep instead of cramming.
lines.zh: 没错。还有，看在老天的份上，好好睡一觉，别临时抱佛脚。

lines.name: Callum
lines.en: Ha, no promises. But seriously, I owe you one. Next coffee's on me.
lines.zh: 哈，不敢保证。不过说真的，我欠你个人情。下次咖啡我请。

phrases.en: I'm a bit of a wreck

phrases.plain: talking too much without a point

phrases.zh: curly在澳洲口语中指刁钻的

phrases.plain: I'll pay you back for this favour
